blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Open sort menu traps keyboard focus: Tab cycles inside it and Escape does not close it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, 2.1.1 Keyboard. A keyboard user opens the menu with Enter on "Sort: …" and focus moves to the first item; pressing Tab or Shift+Tab is prevented and only wraps to another item, and Escape is not handled, so the only way out is to activate an option — the user cannot leave the menu or dismiss it without (re)choosing a sort order, and cannot reach the product list or the rest of the page. Handle Escape to close the menu and return focus to the menu button; let Tab (and Shift+Tab) leave — close the menu without calling preventDefault, as the WAI-ARIA APG menu button pattern does; also close it when focus leaves the list. Alternatively, a native <select> labelled "Sort products" gives all of this for free.
findings.title: Open sort menu traps keyboard focus: Tab cycles inside it and Escape does not close it

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. The expanded state is hard-coded: after a screen reader user activates "Sort: Newest, menu button, collapsed", the menu opens but the button still reports "collapsed", so the state the user hears never matches what is on screen. Bind it to the state — aria-expanded={open}.
findings.title: Menu button always announces aria-expanded="false"
